title: JDBC: the foundation everything else sits on

videos.script: Stop the bookshop and start it again. {{restart}} The book you added a minute ago is gone. Three books, the same three, every time. They lived in a map, and the map died with the process. {{map}} This lesson moves the catalogue into PostgreSQL. A server of its own, which keeps the books when the application stops. {{postgres}} You install it, give the bookshop a role and a database, and learn just enough SQL to make a table. {{sql}} Then you talk to it from Java with nothing in between. A connection, a statement, and the rows, one at a time. That is JDBC, and every library in the next lessons is built on top of it. {{jdbc}} You will see why a value never goes into the text of the SQL. It takes one name with an apostrophe in it. {{quote}} And then the bookshop itself. Spring Boot keeps a pool of open connections, and one small class turns rows into records. {{bookshop}} At the end you restart the application, and the book is still there. {{survives}}
